_note: Notable systems worth visiting. `match` is the exact StarSystem string used for auto-check against the visited-systems set; null means no single-system match (nebula/region) so it stays a manual tick (proximity detection may be added later).

systems.name: Sol
systems.why: Humanity's home system and Earth; permit-locked birthplace of the human race.

systems.name: Sagittarius A*
systems.why: The supermassive black hole at the galactic centre — the ultimate explorer's pilgrimage.

systems.name: Beagle Point
systems.why: One of the most distant reachable systems, endpoint of the first Distant Worlds expedition.

systems.name: Colonia
systems.why: The galaxy's second great hub of humanity, ~22,000 ly from Sol.

systems.name: Explorer's Anchorage (Stuemeae FG-Y d7561)
systems.why: The only major starport near the galactic core.

systems.name: Shinrarta Dezhra
systems.why: Founders World — the exclusive permit-locked home for Elite-rated pilots.

systems.name: California Nebula (NGC 1499)
systems.why: A vast red emission nebula easily reached from inhabited space.

systems.name: Orion Nebula
systems.why: One of the brightest and most famous stellar nurseries, close to the bubble.

systems.name: Barnard's Loop
systems.why: An enormous arc-shaped nebula wrapping around the Orion star-forming region.

systems.name: Rosette Nebula
systems.why: A flower-shaped emission nebula surrounding a cluster of hot young stars.

systems.name: Helix Nebula
systems.why: The iconic 'Eye of God' planetary nebula — a glowing ring of gas.

systems.name: Cat's Paw Nebula
systems.why: A deep-red emission nebula rich in star formation in the Scutum-Centaurus arm.

systems.name: NGC 3199
systems.why: A dramatic crescent-shaped nebula sculpted by a Wolf-Rayet star.

systems.name: Coalsack Nebula
systems.why: A dark nebula ~500 ly from Sol and a notorious Thargoid barnacle hotspot.

systems.name: Horsehead Nebula
systems.why: The famous dark silhouette rising against glowing gas near the Orion complex.

systems.name: Pelican Nebula
systems.why: A sprawling emission nebula neighbouring the North America Nebula.

systems.name: Heart Nebula (IC 1805)
systems.why: A large emission nebula near the Formidine Rift, paired with the Soul Nebula.

systems.name: Soul Nebula (Westerhout 5)
systems.why: The companion glow to the Heart Nebula — a favourite twin-nebula stop.

systems.name: Statue of Liberty Nebula (NGC 3576)
systems.why: Gas clouds that strikingly resemble the Statue of Liberty.

systems.name: Crab Nebula
systems.why: A vividly colourful supernova remnant surrounding the Crab Pulsar.

systems.name: Lagoon Nebula (Messier 8)
systems.why: A bright nebula ringed by neutron stars, black holes and hot stars.

systems.name: Trifid Nebula (Messier 20)
systems.why: A three-lobed blend of emission and reflection nebulosity split by dark dust lanes.

systems.name: Eagle Nebula (Messier 16)
systems.why: Home of the celebrated 'Pillars of Creation'.

systems.name: Bubble Nebula (NGC 7635)
systems.why: A spherical wind-blown bubble near the Heart and Soul Nebulae.

systems.name: Veil Nebula West (NGC 6960)
systems.why: Delicate filaments of an ancient supernova remnant.

systems.name: North America Nebula (NGC 7000)
systems.why: A large emission nebula shaped like the North American continent.

systems.name: Spirograph Nebula (IC 418)
systems.why: A compact planetary nebula with a hot O-type central star.

systems.name: Dumbbell Nebula (Messier 27)
systems.why: A bright, easily reached planetary nebula with a twin-lobed shape.

systems.name: Ring Nebula (Messier 57)
systems.why: The classic glowing smoke-ring planetary nebula.

systems.name: Elephant's Trunk Nebula (IC 1396)
systems.why: A dark, sinuous pillar of dust within a larger emission region.

systems.name: Seagull Nebula (IC 2177)
systems.why: A broad, wing-shaped emission nebula spanning a wide stretch of sky.

systems.name: Thor's Helmet (NGC 2359)
systems.why: A helmet-shaped Wolf-Rayet bubble nebula, one of the galaxy's most photogenic.

systems.name: Running Man Nebula
systems.why: A ghostly blue reflection nebula sitting just above the Orion Nebula.

systems.name: Flame Nebula
systems.why: A bright emission nebula near Alnitak in Orion's belt.

systems.name: Skull and Crossbones Nebula (NGC 2467)
systems.why: An eerie skull-shaped star-forming region.

systems.name: Cave Nebula (Sh2-155)
systems.why: A dim, cavern-like emission and reflection nebula for quieter sightseeing.

systems.name: Iris Nebula
systems.why: A blue reflection nebula illuminated by a bright central star.

systems.name: NGC 1333
systems.why: A dusty reflection nebula and active stellar nursery.

systems.name: Great Annihilator
systems.why: A massive binary black hole near the core, dubbed the 'baby Sagittarius A*'.

systems.name: Jackson's Lighthouse
systems.why: A neutron star close to the bubble with dramatic jets, popular for FSD supercharging.

systems.name: LHS 304
systems.why: A DA white dwarf with vivid blue jet cones — a classic supercharge site.

systems.name: Crab Pulsar
systems.why: A rapidly spinning neutron star at the heart of the Crab Nebula.

systems.name: HD 43162
systems.why: A nearby Sol-like multi-star system, a long-standing exploration waypoint.

systems.name: Merope
systems.why: Central Pleiades system with sprawling Thargoid barnacle forests at Merope 5C.

systems.name: Maia
systems.why: Pleiades hub with meta-alloy trading at Obsidian Orbital and heavy Thargoid activity.

systems.name: Pleione
systems.why: A luminous Pleiades star surrounded by Thargoid interest and barnacle sites.

systems.name: Electra
systems.why: A Pleiades system with Thargoid barnacle fields and non-human signal sources.

systems.name: Celaeno
systems.why: A Pleiades system tied to meta-alloys and persistent Thargoid presence.

systems.name: Asterope
systems.why: A Pleiades star system dotted with Thargoid barnacles.

systems.name: Taygeta
systems.why: A Pleiades system home to heavy alien traffic.

systems.name: Atlas
systems.why: A bright Pleiades star within the Thargoid-contested cluster.

systems.name: HIP 22460
systems.why: Site of one of the first discovered Thargoid surface structures.

systems.name: HIP 17862
systems.why: A Pleiades system linked to Thargoid structures and non-human signals.

systems.name: Witch Head Nebula
systems.why: A haunting reflection nebula near Rigel with an established Thargoid presence.

systems.name: Delphi
systems.why: A Pleiades tourist system central to early Thargoid and Ancient-ruins investigations.

systems.name: Taranis
systems.why: A Thargoid Maelstrom and Titan wreck site from the Thargoid War.

systems.name: Leigong
systems.why: A Thargoid Maelstrom marking a downed Titan — a hotspot for anti-xeno pilots.

systems.name: Synuefe XR-H d11-102
systems.why: The first Ancient Ruins site ever discovered, in October 3302.

systems.name: Synuefe LY-I b42-2
systems.why: Home to a cluster of three Guardian Ancient Ruins sites.

systems.name: Synuefe NL-N c23-4
systems.why: A system containing multiple Guardian Ancient Ruins clusters.

systems.name: Synuefe TP-F b44-0
systems.why: Another triple-cluster Guardian ruins system.

systems.name: Synuefe EU-Q c21-10
systems.why: A confirmed Guardian site identified by Ram Tah's research.

systems.name: Synuefe FM-T d4-32
systems.why: The 'Ancient Plot' Guardian Structure with data terminals and Sentinels.

systems.name: Col 173 Sector QU-O d6-25
systems.why: A Guardian site pinpointed for module and weapon blueprint unlocks.

systems.name: HD 63154
systems.why: One of the Guardian sites confirmed through Ram Tah's decryption work.

systems.name: Lave
systems.why: The iconic trading world of the original 1984 Elite.

systems.name: Diso
systems.why: A classic Elite system famous for Diso Ma Corn.

systems.name: Leesti
systems.why: An original Elite system, home to Azeban City and engineer Didi Vatermann.

systems.name: Reorte
systems.why: A storied system from the original Elite trade routes.

systems.name: Zaonce
systems.why: An original Elite world tied to the galaxy's banking lore.

systems.name: Orrere
systems.why: A classic original-Elite system worth visiting for nostalgia.

systems.name: Azeban
systems.why: One of the founding original-Elite systems.

systems.name: Wolf 359
systems.why: A famously named nearby red dwarf and busy conflict-zone system.

systems.name: Barnard's Star
systems.why: A well-known fast-moving star just a few light-years from Sol.

systems.name: Tau Ceti
systems.why: A nearby Sun-like star and long-inhabited human system.

systems.name: Ross 128
systems.why: A close red-dwarf neighbour of Sol, an easy first hop for new explorers.

systems.name: Alpha Centauri (Hutton Orbital)
systems.why: Home of Hutton Orbital — the infamous ~90-minute supercruise trek and the legendary Hutton mug.

systems.name: Jameson Memorial (Shinrarta Dezhra)
systems.why: The galaxy's premier outfitting station, exclusive to Elite and founding pilots.

systems.name: Jaques Station (Colonia)
systems.why: The station that made the epic 22,000 ly jump that founded Colonia.

systems.name: Obsidian Orbital (Maia)
systems.why: The Pleiades' bustling frontier hub for anti-xeno operations and meta-alloys.

systems.name: Sacaqawea Space Port (Colonia)
systems.why: A major Colonia-region starport and gateway for deep-space travellers.

systems.name: Robigo
systems.why: Home of Robigo Mines — the legendary sightseeing and smuggling passenger-mission hub.

systems.name: Sothis
systems.why: A remote community favourite for lucrative long-range courier and data missions.

systems.name: Ceos
systems.why: Sothis's neighbour, together forming a classic long-haul mission-running pair.

systems.name: Diaguandri (Ray Gateway)
systems.why: A perennial player hub prized for low fees, an engineering broker and easy trade.

systems.name: Semotus Beacon (Oevasy SG-Y d0)
systems.why: The most distant reachable star system from Sol, at the galaxy's very edge.

systems.name: Galactic Aphelion
systems.why: The highest reachable point above the galactic plane, looking down on the whole disc.

systems.name: WISE 0855-0714
systems.why: One of the closest systems to Sol and the coldest known brown dwarf.

systems.name: Rendezvous Point
systems.why: A deep-space expedition waypoint and gathering marker far out in the black.

systems.name: Salomé's Reach
systems.why: A remote memorial honouring the fallen commander Salomé (Kate Bishop).

systems.name: Deciat

systems.name: Wyrd

systems.name: Khun

systems.name: Kuk

systems.name: Laksak

systems.name: Wolf 397

systems.name: Muang
systems.why: Home of Broo Tarquin, engineer for beam, pulse and burst lasers.

systems.name: Yoru
systems.why: Base of Zacariah Nemo, engineer for fragment cannons and multi-cannons.

systems.name: Eurybia
systems.why: Home of Liz Ryder, engineer for missile and torpedo launchers.

systems.name: Arque
systems.why: Base of Professor Palin, a top engineer for thrusters and FSD.

systems.name: Meene
systems.why: Home of Ram Tah, specialist for Guardian module and weapon blueprints.

systems.name: Giryak
systems.why: Base of Juri Ishmaak, engineer for sensors, mines and scanners.

systems.name: Beta-3 Tucani
systems.why: Home of The Sarge, engineer for cannons and drives.

systems.name: Shenve

systems.name: Luchtaine

systems.name: Asura

systems.name: Los

systems.name: Tir

systems.name: Achenar

systems.name: Alioth

systems.name: Sirius

systems.name: Beta Hydri

systems.name: Van Maanen's Star

systems.name: Terra Mater

systems.name: Vega
systems.why: A famous bright star that is permit-locked — a coveted stop for collectors.
